chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

Ali ibn Asbaat wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding a matter of his daughters, and that he could not find anyone like him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'I understood what you mentioned from the matter of your daughters, and that you cannot find anyone like you, but do not wait regarding that, may Allah have Mercy on you, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose mannerisms you are pleased with, and his Religion, so marry to him, or if you do not do it, there would happen strife in the land and a great mischief'.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on delaying marriage when a suitable match is found?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Sahl ibn Ziyad and others, highlights the criteria for selecting a spouse, emphasizing that piety and good character (khuluq) are paramount. It references the Prophet’s warning that neglecting to marry such a person leads to fitnah (strife) and fasad (corruption), a principle often cited in Shia jurisprudence to encourage timely marriage to preserve social stability. The narrative also illustrates the humility of Ali ibn Asbat, who, despite his status, sought guidance on marrying his daughters, reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual compatibility over worldly prestige.
